A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel, real-time fire detection system that can be applied to any conventional video (or static) image stream and can be used in a wide variety of applications including surveillance and disaster management.
we propose a novel extension to the field of automatic fire pixel detection in video and still imagery by combining colour and texture feature descriptors to a classification approach.

we have successfully demonstrated a novel approach to real-time, automatic fire detection that combines colour spectroscopy and texture descriptors to achieve an ∼98% success rate on real-world examples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of texture descriptors in addition to colour spectroscopy can be used to improve the detection of fire regions in real-time.

the use of texture descriptors can be used to extend the scope of existing colour spectroscopy based approaches to fire detection, and that such a combination of features can be used to provide a robust, real-world solution to the problem of fire detection in real-time.

the use of texture descriptors can significantly improve the detection accuracy of fire pixel regions, especially in cases where the fire pixel regions are small and/or the colour of the fire is not easily distinguishable from the background colour.
